knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-8x-23}-2{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=-4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{-8x-23}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-8x-23.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-8.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-8) \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{-8x-23}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{4}{\sqrt{-8x-23}}-6x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-4} & =-\frac{8}{2\sqrt{-8(-4)-23}}-6(-4)^{2} \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}-96 \\  & =-\frac{292}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
